comparisons.coverage_method: Verified all 135 manifest entries, their existence, and the LIBERO suite registry/selectors. Searched the complete inventory for screening, sieving, straining, pouring, shaking, mixtures, and multi-object transfer; then read the closest original BDDL definition in full.
comparisons.objective: The candidate separates ceramic finishing media from steel washers using a supported apertured screen. LIBERO's closest task places one cream-cheese object on a bowl.
comparisons.physical_skill: The candidate requires bimanual load sharing, controlled screen agitation, orientation-dependent passage of multiple free bodies, selective washer retention, tool reseating, and release. LIBERO requires single-object pickup and placement.
comparisons.success_condition: The candidate measures media recovery, requires every washer retained, forbids spill, loss, damage, and invalid passage, and requires a released three-second dwell. LIBERO requires only an On relation.

closest_tasks.name: put_the_cream_cheese_in_the_bowl
closest_tasks.objective: Put one cream-cheese object on a bowl.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Single rigid-object grasp, transport, and receptacle placement.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The cream-cheese object satisfies On cream_cheese_1 akita_black_bowl_1.
closest_tasks.reason: It is the closest receptacle-transfer goal, but has no mixed batch, apertured tool, selective passage, agitation, retained workpieces, or recovery-yield requirement.

comparisons.reason: The complete LIBERO registry contains constituent placement primitives but no task testing physical screening of an intermixed batch while retaining a second object class.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified all 381 manifest entries against the kitchen environment selectors, environment exports, and dataset registry. Reviewed the complete class/docstring inventory for shaking, draining, straining, sorting, pouring, and receptacle transfer, then read the strongest dynamic-tool and transfer neighbors in full.
comparisons.objective: The candidate uses a manual screen to recover finishing media from a washer/media mixture while retaining every washer. RoboCasa's nearest tasks shake a pan containing one vegetable or transfer a vegetable between a pot and sink.
comparisons.physical_skill: ShakePan overlaps in lifting and agitating a loaded vessel while retaining its contents and returning it to a support. DrainVeggies overlaps in receptacle transfer. Neither performs aperture-mediated separation of two intermixed populations or bimanual handling of a loaded screen.
comparisons.success_condition: The candidate grades recovery yield, exact washer retention, spill and damage history, supported replacement, release clearance, and fresh dwell. ShakePan grades accumulated pan motion with the vegetable retained; DrainVeggies grades washing and returning one vegetable.

closest_tasks.name: ShakePan
closest_tasks.objective: Lift and shake a pan containing a vegetable, then return it to the stove.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Loaded-vessel grasping, agitation with content retention, support replacement, and release.
closest_tasks.success_condition: After sufficient qualifying movement, the vegetable remains in the pan and the pan is on the stove.
closest_tasks.reason: It is the closest dynamic-tool task, but rewards generic vessel motion rather than selective aperture passage, bridge clearing, or separation of mixed populations.

closest_tasks.name: DrainVeggies
closest_tasks.quote: return self.vegetables_washed and vegetables_in_pot and not water_on
closest_tasks.objective: Move a vegetable from a pot to a sink, wash it, and return it to the pot.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Receptacle manipulation and transfer of one contained rigid food object.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The vegetable has been washed, is back in the pot, and the water is off.
closest_tasks.reason: It includes contents transfer but does not drain through a perforated implement or separate mixed constituents by geometry.

comparisons.reason: RoboCasa provides meaningful agitation and transfer neighbors, but none tests aperture-mediated granular separation with simultaneous selective retention.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified all 11 manifest entries against the SimplerEnv registration/export files and every inventoried ManiSkill2_real2sim environment source. Read all registered environment implementations represented by the inventory and inspected the closest placement evaluator in full.
comparisons.objective: The candidate screens a two-component mixture already settled in a tool, recovers the smaller media, retains washers, and replaces the screen. SimplerEnv's closest environment puts one source object on or in one target.
comparisons.physical_skill: The shared primitive is terminal object placement. SimplerEnv lacks loaded-tool agitation, bimanual screen handling, many-body flow, orientation-dependent aperture passage, bridge clearing, and selective retention.
comparisons.success_condition: The candidate requires quantitative recovery, zero washer loss, no spill or contamination, screen support, gripper clearance, and fresh dwell. PutOnInSceneEnv succeeds from a one-source/one-target spatial relation.

closest_tasks.name: PutOnInSceneEnv
closest_tasks.objective: Put a selected source object on a selected target object.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Single rigid-object grasping, transport, alignment, and supported placement.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The source is geometrically above and within the target footprint without disallowed significant contact.
closest_tasks.reason: It covers only an ordinary terminal placement primitive and does not model a loaded screen, multiple free contents, selective passage, agitation, loss, or recovery yield.

comparisons.reason: The complete SimplerEnv registry has no plausible task-level overlap with controlled physical screening.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified all 1,122 manifest entries and both repositories' recorded activity-definition and backend selectors. Searched the complete activity inventory for sieves, screens, pouring, draining, sorting, mixtures, and granular transfer; then read the closest definitions and relevant predicate implementation in full. The sieve activity's actual goal is cleanliness, not filtering.
comparisons.objective: The candidate physically separates ceramic media from steel washers through an apertured screen. BEHAVIOR includes cleaning a sieve and pouring water into a glass, but neither uses a sieve to separate a mixture.
comparisons.physical_skill: CleanASieve removes a covering state from a tool; PouringWaterInAGlass transfers one substance between containers. The candidate depends on rigid-body geometry, controlled agitation, orientation-dependent aperture passage, bridge clearing, and retention of a second population.
comparisons.success_condition: The candidate requires at least 98% recovery for completion credit, every washer retained, no loss or contamination, supported release, and revocable dwell. CleanASieve requires removal of covered; PouringWaterInAGlass requires a glass on a counter and filled with water.

closest_tasks.name: clean_a_sieve-0
closest_tasks.objective: Remove adhesive material covering a sieve.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Cleaning a tool surface using water, soap, and a sponge.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The sieve is no longer covered by the adhesive material.
closest_tasks.reason: The shared sieve noun does not establish ability overlap: its holes never filter a mixture, and its goal measures cleanliness rather than selective passage or recovery.

closest_tasks.name: pouring_water_in_a_glass-0
closest_tasks.objective: Place a water glass on a countertop and fill it with water from a pitcher.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The glass is on the countertop and satisfies the filled relation with water.
closest_tasks.reason: It overlaps in contents transfer but has no retained second constituent, aperture interaction, bridge clearing, or recovery-yield requirement.

comparisons.reason: Inspection of the actual sieve goal and predicate-backed activities found no BEHAVIOR task testing physical screening of an intermixed batch.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified both manifest files and the authoritative ten-task Tier-1 catalog. Read all ten setup, instruction, reset, and scoring records in official-setups.json and checked their linked procedure records in official-procedures.json; the catalog explicitly enumerates every published task ID.
comparisons.objective: The candidate performs post-finishing bulk separation and media recovery using a manual screen. DataCenterBench covers switches, covers, a keypad, connectors, a slider, and cable routing; its nearest task is a bimanual connector join.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both require coordinated bimanual contact. DC-join stabilizes a coupler while aligning and inserting one plug. The candidate shares a changing loaded screen between grippers, agitates multiple bodies through apertures, prevents spill, retains washers, and reseats the tool.
comparisons.success_condition: The candidate uses fractional recovery, exact retention, damage and loss disqualifiers, and released dwell. DC-join is binary and succeeds when a plug is fully inserted without a gap.

closest_tasks.name: DC-join — Join the Ethernet plug and coupler
closest_tasks.quote: Use one hand to hold the Ethernet coupler and the other to insert the Ethernet plug into it until it clicks into place.
closest_tasks.objective: Stabilize an Ethernet coupler and insert a plug until seated and latched.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Bimanual stabilization, connector alignment, axial insertion, and latch engagement.
closest_tasks.success_condition: The Ethernet plug is fully inserted into the coupler with no gap.
closest_tasks.reason: It is the strongest bimanual-contact neighbor, but has no bulk contents, tool agitation, selective passage, recovery, or retained workpiece population.

comparisons.reason: No DataCenterBench task tests pouring, screening, granular separation, or recovery; the closest task shares only general bimanual coordination.

comparisons.coverage_method: Verified all 110 manifest entries against every recorded task, configuration, and task-registry selector. Reviewed the complete inventory for pouring, sorting, shaking, containers, granular objects, and release, then read the closest multi-object pouring Python and YAML definitions in full.
comparisons.objective: The candidate begins with ceramic media and washers settled together in a screen and selectively passes the media through apertures while retaining the washers. RoboDojo's nearest task pours seven balls from a cup into a vase.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both require controlling multiple free rigid bodies, avoiding spill or jams, restoring a manipulated tool, and releasing it. The candidate additionally requires bimanual loaded-screen handling, selective passage of only one population, deliberate bridge clearing, and washer retention.
comparisons.success_condition: The candidate gives recovery-based partial credit, requires at least 98% recovery for completion credit and complete washer retention, and permanently invalidates spill, contamination, damage, or tunneled passage. PourBallsIntoVase requires all seven balls in the vase, the cup upright, and the robot at origin.

closest_tasks.name: pour_balls_into_vase
closest_tasks.quote: Pour all the balls from the cup into the vase.
closest_tasks.objective: Pour seven balls from a cup into a vase, then restore and release the cup.
closest_tasks.physical_skill: Multi-body rigid pouring through a restricted opening, avoidance of misses or mouth jams, and tool replacement.
closest_tasks.success_condition: All seven spheres are inside the vase, the cup is upright, and the robot has returned to origin.
closest_tasks.reason: This is substantive overlap in controlled multi-body flow, but its endpoint is complete transfer of one homogeneous population rather than physical classification with simultaneous retention of a second population.

comparisons.reason: RoboDojo contains a real granular-transfer neighbor, but the candidate's central ability is aperture-based separation of two intermixed populations, not transfer of every particle to one receptacle.
